raw_case_text:
An 8-year-old girl, from a rural area in Choco (Colombian Pacific Coast), presented with 20 days of fever, hiporexia, asthenia, and arthralgias, associated with emesis and diarrhea. She was found to have anemia and was prescribed ferrous bisglycinate without improvement. The fever was persistent and was associated with chills, abdominal pain, and dark urine; she was admitted to a rural hospital and diagnosed with pancytopenia; 2 units of packed red blood cells were transfused; and she was transferred to our hospital with a clinical suspicion of lymphoproliferative disorder. Her vital signs showed tachycardia (131 bpm), tachypnea (45 per min), and limit-low oxygen saturation (91%). Physical examination revealed jaundice and hepatosplenomegaly of 6 cm and of 2 cm below the costal margin, respectively; fine right basal crackles and a soft systolic heart murmur were heard at the left sternal border and the third intercostal space. Her past medical history was relevant for posttraumatic osteomyelitis of the right humerus and septic arthritis of the right elbow; her parents were not consanguineous, and she did not have pseudoalbinism.
Test results revealed thrombocytopenia and lymphopenia (Hg 11.5 g/dL, WBCs 4600/microL, neutrophils 3404/microL, lymphocytes 1058/microL, and platelets 59000/microL), elevated C-reactive protein (21.57 mg/dL), and altered liver function tests (ALT 349 U/L, AST 135 U/L, total bilirubin 6.67 mg/dL, direct bilirubin 5.3 mg/dL, LDH 1376 IU/L, and albumin 2.1 g/dL). Infectious workup was negative for HIV, dengue, malaria, Hepatitis B, Hepatitis C, CMV, EBV, and Mycoplasma. Additional laboratory tests showed hypertriglyceridemia (787 mg/dL) and hyperferritinemia (>2000 ng/mL) with normal fibrinogen (311 mg/dL). Echocardiogram showed minimal pericardial effusion and preserved ventricular function without anatomic defects or signs of endocarditis. Abdominal ultrasound showed a small right pleural effusion, hepatomegaly, splenomegaly, and retroperitoneal and hepatic hilar lymphadenopathies. Abdominal computed tomography showed the same findings, with hypodensity areas corresponding to splenic infarcts. She was diagnosed with hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis and started on piperacillin-tazobactam and intravenous immunoglobulin (1 g/kg/d for 2 days); while waiting for blood cultures and bone marrow analysis, CSF was within normal limits. On her third hospital night, she presented hematemesis and rectorrhagia with hypovolemic shock that required fluid resuscitation, intravenous infusion of omeprazole, tranexamic acid, phytomenadione, packed red blood cell, and platelets transfusion. She was stabilized; upper and lower endoscopies did not show signs of active bleeding, but just some residual melena. On the fourth day of hospitalization, both blood and bone marrow cultures were positive for Salmonella typhi; and the antibiotic regimen was changed to ciprofloxacin; bone marrow specimen showed hematopoietic precursors with no signs of malignancy; and no hemophagocytosis was appreciated. Repeated blood cultures were negative; during the hospital stay, she was started on enalapril to maintain a tight control on blood pressure. She completed 14 days of antibiotic treatment with resolution of the fever, hepatomegaly, splenomegaly, and the abdominal pain. Laboratory investigations before discharge showed resolution of the cytopenias, down trending of liver function tests and triglycerides levels, and ferritin was still elevated.

subjective.chief_complaint: An 8-year-old girl presented with 20 days of persistent fever, hyporexia, asthenia, and arthralgias, associated with vomiting and diarrhea.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Symptoms began 20 days prior with fever, hyporexia, asthenia, arthralgias, emesis, and diarrhea. She was diagnosed with anemia and given ferrous bisglycinate without improvement. Persistent fever was accompanied by chills, abdominal pain, and dark urine. At a rural hospital, she was diagnosed with pancytopenia and transfused 2 units of packed red blood cells before transfer. On hospital night 3, she developed hematemesis and rectorrhagia with hypovolemic shock.
subjective.past_medical_history: Past medical history significant for posttraumatic osteomyelitis of the right humerus and septic arthritis of the right elbow. Non-consanguineous parents; no pseudoalbinism. Resides in a rural area in Chocó (Colombian Pacific Coast). Received 2 units packed red blood cells at referring facility.
subjective.review_of_systems: Chills, dark urine, hematemesis, rectorrhagia, arthralgias. Home medication: ferrous bisglycinate.

objective.physical_examination: Jaundice present. Tachycardia (pulse rate 131 bpm), tachypnea (respiratory rate 45/min), borderline low SpO2 (91%). Cardiovascular: soft systolic heart murmur at left sternal border and 3rd intercostal space. Respiratory: fine right basal crackles. Abdomen: hepatomegaly (6 cm below costal margin) and splenomegaly (2 cm below costal margin).
objective.routine_investigations: Hemoglobin: 11.5 g/dL (post-transfusion); WBC count: 4,600/microL (neutrophils 3,404/microL, lymphocytes 1,058/microL); platelets: 59,000/microL. C-reactive protein: elevated at 21.57 mg/dL. Ferritin: >2,000 ng/mL; triglycerides: 787 mg/dL; fibrinogen: 311 mg/dL. LFTs: ALT 349 U/L, AST 135 U/L, total bilirubin 6.67 mg/dL, direct bilirubin 5.3 mg/dL, LDH 1,376 IU/L, albumin 2.1 g/dL. Infectious workup: HIV, dengue, malaria, Hepatitis B, Hepatitis C, CMV, EBV, and Mycoplasma all negative. Abdominal ultrasound: small right pleural effusion, hepatomegaly, splenomegaly, retroperitoneal and hepatic hilar lymphadenopathies. Echocardiogram: minimal pericardial effusion, preserved ventricular function, no endocarditis.
objective.advanced_workup: Abdominal CT: hepatosplenomegaly, retroperitoneal and hepatic hilar lymphadenopathies, small right pleural effusion, and hypodensity areas corresponding to splenic infarcts. Lumbar puncture: CSF within normal limits. Bone marrow analysis: hematopoietic precursors with no signs of malignancy and no hemophagocytosis. Upper and lower endoscopy: no signs of active bleeding; residual melena present.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Definitive diagnosis: Typhoid fever due to Salmonella enterica serotype Typhi, complicated by secondary hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH), gastrointestinal hemorrhage with hypovolemic shock, and splenic infarcts. Confirmed on hospital day 4 by positive blood and bone marrow cultures for Salmonella typhi (repeat blood cultures were negative). Initially treated empirically with intravenous piperacillin-tazobactam and IVIG (1 g/kg/day for 2 days). Hypovolemic shock managed with fluid resuscitation, IV omeprazole, tranexamic acid, phytomenadione, PRBCs, and platelet transfusions. Following culture confirmation, antibiotics were switched to ciprofloxacin to complete 14 days of therapy, and enalapril was initiated for blood pressure control. Achieved resolution of fever, hepatomegaly, splenomegaly, and abdominal pain. Pre-discharge testing showed resolution of cytopenias, downtrending transaminases and triglycerides; ferritin remained elevated.
